chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: How Basie and Ellington let people go; Basie's luck
summary: Basie let sidemen eliminate themselves through others; he lets others handle everything, which Royal calls luck.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You spent such a long time with Basie

Well, not quite as much personnel change as you might think. In the course of 20 years, Basie doesn't fire many people. He usually makes people sort of eliminate themselves. He, as it was with the Ellington band, he sort of did the same thing. Ellington let people sort of eliminate themselves. After they just piled it up so high that they couldn't see over the top of it, well, then, that was the end.
How does Basie do it? I know how Duke does it (inaudible).

Oh, the same way with Basie. He's a little easy. He isn't a guy that comes out and says too much about anything. He's a little bit chicken that way. But he'll -- he has his own sly little way that he will eventually find a way to let them go, if the time comes.
Well, is he a manipulator, like Duke is?
No, he doesn't manipulate that way at all. He is a lie-low guy. He lays way back and lets other people do his dirty work for him.

Would he -- like, how would he let somebody let themselves go? I mean, Duke would have a variety of ways. I don't think he ever did it the same way with any two people. But toward the end, he would make life so miserable for somebody, they were happier being (inaudible).

No, Basie wasn't a heckler. He wasn't that way. He would just sort of let a guy go until he realized himself that he wasn't welcome there and the guys in the band would do his dirty work for him. They'd heckle and do a little undercover work for him and did it that way. And all of a --

No, they -- I don't know. It's hard to explain those sort of things. Basie always let somebody else do practically everything for him, except plink, plink, plink on the end of his solos. He's a fellow that does very, very little for himself. He's got somebody that takes care of everything one way or the other.

See, like in Duke's band, Duke write the music. He would do some of the manipulating and foster a few ideas and things. But Basie -- somebody else -- he just laid cool and worked on his racing forms and let somebody else do whatever there was to do.
But (inaudible) having the good sense to hire somebody like you to run the band?
I don't know whether it was good sense or whether he was just lucky.
Some people are just very fortunate. Some people, it's best that you don't try to find out and pin them down to what they do. Some people are gifted with a little thing in their

life that carries them straight on through, just like a drunk man falling down a step. You could fall down a double flight of steps and break your back and have contusions and concussions. A drunk man could fall down a complete flight of steps and never get a bruise. Some people are just lucky.
And you think Basie's been just lucky?
